title: Best practices for Claude Code
author: Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's own playbook for Claude Code. It is built on one idea: the context window fills fast and quality drops as it fills. From there it covers giving Claude a check it can run, splitting explore-plan-implement-commit, writing a short CLAUDE.md, and scaling out with non-interactive mode, worktrees and an adversarial review subagent.
who_for: Developers who installed Claude Code, use it daily, and still get mediocre results.
skip_if: Skip if you have never used a terminal, or if you want an install walkthrough. This page assumes Claude Code already runs and jumps straight to technique.
notes: Read end to end on 2026-08-21. No publish date on the page; it is a living doc and currently reflects auto mode, /goal, agent teams and dynamic workflows. A plain-markdown copy is at the same URL with .md appended, which is useful for feeding to an agent.

title: Hooks reference (Claude Code)
author: Anthropic
summary: The complete reference for Claude Code hooks: every lifecycle event, the JSON input and output schema, exit codes, and the async, HTTP, prompt and MCP-tool hook variants.
who_for: Developers who want deterministic enforcement, such as lint after every edit or blocking writes to a path, instead of advisory rules in CLAUDE.md that Claude can ignore.
skip_if: Skip if you are still learning the basics. Read the hooks guide first. This is a lookup reference, not a tutorial, and it is enormous.
notes: Not read in full. The markdown source is about 280 KB, the largest page in the Claude Code docs, so this is listed rather than previewed. Confirmed live on 2026-08-21.

title: Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions
author: Anthropic
summary: How to run several Claude Code instances as a team, with one lead, a shared task list and direct teammate-to-teammate messaging. Includes a straight comparison with subagents on context, communication and token cost.
who_for: Developers who have hit the ceiling of one session and are considering parallel agents for research, cross-layer features, or competing debugging hypotheses.
skip_if: Skip unless the task truly splits into independent pieces. Teams cost far more tokens than one session, and for sequential work or same-file edits a single session or subagents win.
notes: Read the opening and the comparison tables on 2026-08-21. The feature is experimental and off by default: you must set CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1. The page documents behaviour as of v2.1.178 and lists known limitations around resumption and shutdown.

title: Choose a sandbox environment for Claude Code
author: Anthropic
summary: Compares six ways to isolate Claude Code, from the built-in sandboxed Bash tool through sandbox runtime, dev containers, custom containers, virtual machines and Claude Code on the web, by what each actually contains and what it costs to set up.
who_for: Anyone about to run Claude Code unattended, in auto mode, or against a repository they do not fully trust.
skip_if: Skip if you only run short supervised sessions on your own code and approve each action yourself. The setup effort will not pay for itself.
notes: Read the comparison tables and warnings on 2026-08-21. Usefully blunt: a sandbox reduces blast radius but is not a hard control, and isolation does not change what gets sent to the model.

title: Agent SDK overview
author: Anthropic
summary: The entry point for building your own agent on the same loop that powers Claude Code, in Python or TypeScript. The value is the decision table: when to use the Agent SDK versus the CLI, the Client SDK, or Managed Agents.
who_for: Developers who want Claude Code's harness, meaning its tools, context management, subagents, hooks and MCP support, as a library inside their own product.
skip_if: Skip if you only use Claude Code interactively. Skip also if you want raw model access and intend to write the tool loop yourself, in which case the Client SDK is the right choice.
notes: Read end to end on 2026-08-21. Short page. Two things people miss: claude.ai login and subscription rate limits are not permitted for third-party agents built on the SDK, and you may not brand your product as Claude Code.

title: Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock
author: Anthropic
summary: Setup for running Claude Code against models in your own AWS account: the /setup-bedrock wizard, the use case form, IAM permissions, the AWS credential chain, region selection, and pinning model versions before a team rollout.
who_for: Engineers in organisations that must keep model traffic inside AWS for IAM, billing, network or compliance reasons.
skip_if: Skip if you are an individual on a Pro or Max plan. You gain nothing and take on a lot of AWS configuration.
notes: Read prerequisites and the setup steps on 2026-08-21. Sibling pages exist for Google Cloud's Agent Platform (renamed from Vertex AI) and Microsoft Foundry; note the rename, since older tutorials still say Vertex AI.

title: Skill authoring best practices
author: Anthropic
summary: How to write a SKILL.md that Claude finds and uses well: treat the context window as a public good, assume Claude is already smart, split long skills across files with progressive disclosure, and test with real usage.
who_for: Developers packaging team knowledge or a repeatable workflow as a skill for Claude Code, the API or the Agent SDK.
skip_if: Skip if you have not written a skill yet; read the Skills overview first. Skip also if your need is a one-off prompt rather than a reusable workflow.
notes: Read the core principles section on 2026-08-21. Concrete because it shows good and bad versions with approximate token counts. Since Agent Skills is now an open standard, this advice also transfers to other agents that read SKILL.md.

title: Claude Managed Agents overview
author: Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's hosted agent harness. You define an agent, an environment (an Anthropic cloud sandbox or a self-hosted one) and sessions; Anthropic runs the loop, the sandbox, tool execution, compaction and caching.
who_for: Teams that want long-running, scheduled or asynchronous agents without building their own loop, sandbox and session store.
skip_if: Skip if you need Zero Data Retention or a HIPAA BAA. Managed Agents is stateful by design and is not eligible for either. Skip also if you want full control of the agent loop; use the Messages API instead.
notes: Read end to end on 2026-08-21. Still in beta: every endpoint needs the managed-agents-2026-04-01 header, and MCP tunnels and 'dreams' sit behind a narrower research preview you must request.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
author: Anthropic Engineering
summary: Argues that context engineering replaces prompt engineering once an agent runs over many turns, and gives a mental model for curating the whole context state (system prompt, tools, history, retrieved data) rather than just wording a prompt.
who_for: Developers building agents that run for many turns and get worse as the context fills.
skip_if: Skip if you only make single-turn API calls. Read the July 2026 follow-up first if you are on Claude 5 generation models, because it reverses several recommendations here.
notes: About 11 months old, so possibly outdated by this audience's standards. Still the clearest statement of the framework, but partly superseded by 'The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models' (2026-07-24). Read the opening sections on 2026-08-21.

title: Writing effective tools for agents - with agents
author: Anthropic Engineering
summary: How to design tools an agent can actually use: namespacing, the shape of return values, token budgets, and building an evaluation so you can point Claude Code at your own tool definitions and have it optimise them against that eval.
who_for: Anyone shipping an MCP server or custom tools whose agent keeps calling them wrong or wastefully.
skip_if: Skip if you only consume other people's tools and never write your own.
notes: About 11 months old. By Ken Aizawa with Anthropic's Research, MCP and Product Engineering teams. Read the opening and principles list on 2026-08-21. Most of it holds, but check the advice on putting examples in tool descriptions against the 2026 context-engineering post, which now argues examples over-constrain newer models.

title: Code execution with MCP: building more efficient agents
author: Anthropic Engineering
summary: Names the failure mode of loading hundreds of MCP tool definitions into context and passing every intermediate result through the model, then shows the alternative: present MCP servers as a code API on a filesystem and let the agent write short programs against them.
who_for: Developers whose agent has become slow and expensive because it is wired to dozens of MCP servers.
skip_if: Skip if you connect two or three MCP servers. The pattern requires a code execution sandbox, which is a real security surface you then have to own.
notes: About 9 months old. The widely quoted '150k tokens down to 2k' figure comes from one worked example in this post, not from a general benchmark; treat it as an illustration. Read the problem statement and setup on 2026-08-21.

title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
author: Anthropic Engineering
summary: Sets out the vocabulary of agent evaluation - task, trial, grader, transcript, outcome - and explains why multi-turn agents have to be graded on the final state of the environment rather than on matching output text.
who_for: Teams that keep shipping agent regressions because they have no repeatable test, and anyone who has to prove an agent got better.
skip_if: Skip if you have not shipped an agent yet; it will read as abstract. Skip if you want a ready-made eval framework, because this is concepts and worked reasoning, not code.
notes: Published 2026-01-09. One of very few first-party pieces on agent evals, which is a genuine gap in developer content. Read the definitions and examples section on 2026-08-21.

title: How we contain Claude across products
author: Anthropic Engineering
summary: Anthropic's own account of capping agent blast radius across claude.ai, Claude Code and Cowork. It admits permission prompts largely failed (telemetry showed users approving about 93 percent of them) and walks through what sandboxes, VMs and egress controls actually buy you.
who_for: Engineers responsible for letting an agent touch real infrastructure, and anyone writing an internal policy for agentic tools.
skip_if: Skip if you want configuration steps. This is architecture and postmortem thinking, not something you can copy into settings.json.
notes: Published 2026-05-25 and currently the featured post on Anthropic's engineering blog. Unusually candid about security failures they hit, including Claude 'helpfully' escaping a sandbox. Read most of the body on 2026-08-21, not the closing sections.

title: The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models
author: Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic
summary: Anthropic deleted over 80 percent of Claude Code's system prompt for Claude 5 models with no measurable eval loss. The post turns that into five reversals: stop writing rules, stop giving examples, stop front-loading everything, stop repeating yourself, and stop hand-writing memory into CLAUDE.md.
who_for: Anyone maintaining a long CLAUDE.md, a large skill library, or a custom agent harness that was tuned for older models.
skip_if: Skip if you are pinned to older Claude models. The advice is explicitly tied to the Claude 5 generation and removing guardrails can hurt on earlier ones.
notes: Published 2026-07-24; the page states a 5 minute read. Read end to end on 2026-08-21. Points at the /doctor command in Claude Code, which audits your own config for over-constraining and duplicated rules. This is the single most useful item here if your setup is old.

title: Maximizing the value of your Claude Code sessions
author: Lydia Hallie, Anthropic
summary: The clearest explanation anywhere of what a Claude Code turn actually costs: prefill versus decode, how the prompt cache is keyed, and exactly which actions (/model, /effort, fast mode, /compact, an hour of idle time) throw the cache away mid-conversation.
who_for: Developers burning through plan limits or an API budget who cannot see where the tokens go.
skip_if: Skip if cost is not a constraint for you. The workflow advice on its own is already covered in the best-practices page.
notes: Published 2026-08-14 by a member of the Claude Code team; page states a 5 minute read. Read end to end on 2026-08-21. Freshest item in this set. Some details are version-pinned (for example /autocompact needs v2.1.221+), so they will date quickly.

title: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code
author: Thariq Shihipar and Sid Bidasaria, Anthropic
summary: Explains dynamic workflows, where Claude writes its own JavaScript orchestration harness over subagents, and names six reusable patterns: classify-and-act, fan-out-and-synthesise, adversarial verification, generate-and-filter, tournament, and loop-until-done.
who_for: Developers running large migrations, codebase audits, triage queues, flaky-test hunts, or anything where one context window drifts, quits early, or grades its own work.
skip_if: Skip for ordinary coding tasks. The post says so itself: workflows use far more tokens, and most work does not need a panel of five reviewers.
notes: Published 2026-06-02; page states a 5 minute read. Read end to end on 2026-08-21. The most valuable part is naming the three failure modes it fixes: agentic laziness, self-preferential bias and goal drift. Includes a 'when not to use this' section, which is rare.

title: Claude Code 101
author: Anthropic (Claude Academy)
summary: Anthropic's own onboarding course for Claude Code: installing it across terminal, VS Code, JetBrains, Desktop and web, then the Explore - Plan - Code - Commit loop, permission and plan modes, code review, and the context commands that keep long sessions usable.
who_for: Engineers who have not used an agentic coding tool before and want the official mental model instead of a random YouTube walkthrough.
skip_if: Skip if you already use Claude Code daily; go straight to the best-practices page. Reported to require a Pro, Max or Enterprise plan or an API key for the hands-on exercises.
notes: Anthropic's courses moved from anthropic.skilljar.com to academy.claude.com; old links redirect, so prefer this URL. The course page is client-rendered, so lesson count and runtime could not be read directly and the time given here is an estimate. Free with an email signup; certificate on completion.

title: Building with the Claude API
author: Anthropic (Claude Academy)
summary: The largest course on Claude Academy: 67 lessons and 8 quizzes covering prompting, tool use, retrieval, agents, MCP and production patterns against the Claude API, in one ordered path.
who_for: Backend and platform engineers integrating Claude into a product who want a single structured route rather than jumping around the reference docs.
skip_if: Skip if you only use Claude Code and never touch the API. Nine hours is a real commitment, and if you learn by reading code the cookbooks get you there faster.
notes: Lesson count (67), quiz count (8) and the 9 hour runtime were read from the Claude Platform listing on academy.claude.com on 2026-08-21. Course content itself not previewed. Free with an email signup.

title: Model Context Protocol: Advanced Topics
author: Anthropic (Claude Academy)
summary: The follow-on to Anthropic's introductory MCP course, going past the tools, resources and prompts primitives into the harder parts of building and shipping MCP servers.
who_for: Developers who already built a basic MCP server and have run into transport, authentication or scale questions.
skip_if: Skip if you have not built an MCP server at all; do the introductory course first. Skip if you only install other people's servers rather than writing your own.
notes: Listed on academy.claude.com as 11 lessons and 1 quiz; no runtime shown, so the time here is an estimate. Content not previewed because the course page is client-rendered and behind a signup. One of the very few 'advanced MCP' offerings from a first-party source.

title: Agent Skills with Anthropic
author: Elie Schoppik (Anthropic) on DeepLearning.AI
summary: Builds skills from scratch and runs the same ones in four places - claude.ai, Claude Code, the Claude API and the Agent SDK - and spends real time on how skills differ from tools, MCP and subagents, and on progressive disclosure to keep them cheap.
who_for: Developers who want one reusable format for team knowledge that also works in Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents that read SKILL.md.
skip_if: Skip if you want depth on one surface; this course deliberately spreads across four. It is labelled Beginner, so it will feel slow if you already write skills.
notes: Page states Beginner, 2h19m, 10 video lessons, 1 graded assignment, taught by Elie Schoppik. Full syllabus read on 2026-08-21. No publish date shown. Cost caveat: the button said 'Enroll Now' rather than 'Enroll for Free' as on the sibling Claude Code course, so confirm whether a PRO membership is needed for more than the certificate.

title: Claude Code: A Highly Agentic Coding Assistant
author: Elie Schoppik (Anthropic) on DeepLearning.AI
summary: Three real projects instead of a feature tour: explore and extend a RAG chatbot codebase, refactor a Jupyter notebook into a dashboard, and build a web app from a Figma mockup using the Figma and Playwright MCP servers.
who_for: Developers comfortable with Python and git who learn by building, and who want a guided path through CLAUDE.md, plan mode, subagents, worktrees, hooks and the GitHub integration.
skip_if: Skip if you do not know Python and git. Skip if you need current feature coverage: the syllabus predates auto mode, agent teams and dynamic workflows, so check anything about commands or flags against the docs.
notes: Page states Intermediate, 2h, 10 video lessons, 1 graded assignment, 'Enroll for Free'. Full syllabus read on 2026-08-21. No publish date on the page, which is the main risk with it.

title: Claude Code (Frontend Masters)
author: Lydia Hallie, Anthropic
summary: A workshop by an engineer on the Claude Code team. It starts from the model and the harness, then works through permission modes, effort and model selection, CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, subagents, agent teams, plugins, MCP and the Agent SDK.
who_for: Working developers who want the under-the-hood mental model plus the newer features that most 2025-era tutorials never mention.
skip_if: Skip if you want deep API or SDK work; this is about Claude Code the tool. Needs a free account, and 1.9 hours is tight for that many topics, so expect breadth over depth in places.
notes: Page states 16 lessons, 1.9 hours, 4.7 rating, free with signup, certificate on completion. Full curriculum read on 2026-08-21. Frontend Masters now brands the site as Master.dev, but the frontendmasters.com URL still resolves. No publish date shown; the syllabus mentions agent teams, so it is recent.

title: anthropics/claude-quickstarts
author: Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's collection of runnable starter projects for building deployable applications on the Claude API. Clone one, add your key, and read working code rather than reference docs.
who_for: Developers who need to run something first and read the reference afterwards.
skip_if: Skip if you want explanation. These are projects with minimal narration. Skip if your work is Claude Code workflows rather than API integration.
notes: 17,487 stars, last push 2026-08-19 (checked via the GitHub API on 2026-08-21). Actively maintained, not a stale high-star trap. Repo contents not reviewed.

title: anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python
author: Anthropic
summary: The official Python Agent SDK source, changelog and issue tracker. In a fast-moving SDK this is often the quickest way to find out what actually changed and what currently works.
who_for: Python developers building on the Agent SDK who need real behaviour rather than documented behaviour.
skip_if: Skip if you work in TypeScript; use anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript instead. Skip if you want tutorials, because the docs site is the better starting point.
notes: 7,942 stars, last push 2026-08-20 (checked via the GitHub API on 2026-08-21). The Python package bundles the Claude Code CLI, so no separate install is needed. Repo contents not reviewed.

title: anthropics/claude-code-action
author: Anthropic
summary: The official GitHub Action that runs Claude Code in CI: responding to @claude mentions on issues and pull requests, reviewing diffs, turning issues into PRs, or running headless on a schedule.
who_for: Teams that want Claude in the pull request loop rather than only on one developer's laptop.
skip_if: Skip if you are not on GitHub; see the GitLab CI/CD docs instead. Skip until you have a token budget and a review policy, because this runs unattended against your repository.
notes: 8,677 stars, last push 2026-08-20 (checked via the GitHub API on 2026-08-21). Built on the Agent SDK. The repo docs include a solutions guide with worked workflow examples for review, triage and doc sync. Contents not reviewed.

title: ClaudeLog
author: InventorBlack (OpenCues)
summary: The largest independent Claude Code knowledge base. Mechanics pages on plan mode, ultrathink, context inspection, dynamic memory, output styles and permutation frameworks, plus a CLAUDE.md vault, an MCP section and a long FAQ.
who_for: Developers who want community-tested techniques and blunt opinions that a vendor doc will never print.
skip_if: Skip if you need authoritative answers. This is one person's experiments, it is not affiliated with Anthropic, and individual pages carry no visible date, so verify anything about flags or commands against the official docs first.
notes: Site index browsed on 2026-08-21. Maintained by InventorBlack, a moderator of r/ClaudeAI. The homepage references current models (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 5), so the site is being kept current overall, but per-page freshness is hard to judge, which is its main weakness.

title: Agentic Engineering Patterns
author: Simon Willison
summary: A growing, deliberately evergreen guide of named patterns for working with coding agents: writing code is cheap now, red/green TDD, agentic manual testing, subagent use, git practice, and linear walkthroughs for understanding unfamiliar code.
who_for: Experienced engineers who want practice-level patterns that are not tied to one vendor's feature list, and who want a clear line drawn between agentic engineering and vibe coding.
skip_if: Skip if you want Claude-specific configuration; it covers OpenAI Codex too and stays tool-agnostic on purpose. Skip if you need a finished book, because chapters are still being added.
notes: Announced 2026-02-23; chapters are updated in place rather than frozen, so treat that as a start date, not a freshness date. Full chapter list and introduction read on 2026-08-21. Willison states the prose is written by him, not generated.

title: Code w/ Claude Developer Conference (session recordings)
author: Anthropic
summary: Full session recordings from Anthropic's developer conference: keynotes plus breakouts from the teams that build Claude Code, the Agent SDK and MCP, and from customers running agents in production.
who_for: Developers who want the design reasoning straight from the people who shipped the features, rather than a third-party summary.
skip_if: Skip if you want a tutorial. These are conference talks, not walkthroughs, and any live demo of a specific flag or command may already be out of date.
notes: Playlist title is 'Code w/ Claude Developer Conference' on the @claude channel. It is not year-scoped, so it may mix the 2025 and 2026 events; check each video's date before trusting a demo. Verified live on 2026-08-21. Individual videos not watched.

title: Build an MCP server
author: Model Context Protocol project
summary: The primary tutorial for writing your first MCP server end to end - a weather server exposing two tools - and connecting it to a host, with separate Python and TypeScript paths.
who_for: Developers who want to expose their own system or data to Claude and other agents instead of only installing other people's servers.
skip_if: Skip if you only want to connect existing MCP servers; the Claude Code MCP quickstart is faster. Skip if you have no local Python or Node toolchain to work in.
notes: Vendor-neutral primary source rather than an aggregator, which matters because MCP now has many competing tutorial sites. Spec and docs are maintained at modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol on GitHub: 9,010 stars, last push 2026-08-20 (checked 2026-08-21). No publish date on the page; the docs are versioned and updated.

title: Head of Claude Code: What happens after coding is solved (Boris Cherny)
author: Lenny Rachitsky with Boris Cherny (Anthropic)
summary: The person who created Claude Code on how he now works, including not hand-editing code since November 2025, how the tool went from an internal hack to a large share of public GitHub commits, and where he thinks software engineering goes next.
who_for: Senior engineers and team leads deciding how far to push agentic workflows, and who want the argument from the source rather than from a commentator.
skip_if: Skip if you want technique. There is almost nothing here you can copy into your terminal, and the framing is aimed at product and career questions as much as engineering ones.
notes: Publish date 2026-02-19 verified from the page's datePublished metadata on 2026-08-21. Roughly 1 hour 28 minutes according to third-party listings; duration not verified directly. Not listened to, so claims made in the episode are not checked here.
